holidays.name: Star Wars Day (May the Fourth Be With You Day)
holidays.description: Fans around the galaxy greet each other with "May the Fourth be with you." They marathon the movies, dress as Jedi and Sith, and quote Yoda all day long. It's a pun-powered holiday that turns a calendar date into a lightsaber-waving party.
holidays.origin: The holiday comes from a pun on the saying "May the Force be with you." Fans began using the phrase informally for years. It got a boost in 2011 when a Toronto fan celebration made the day official among fans. Lucasfilm and Disney have since embraced it with annual releases and events.
holidays.funFact: The pun is older than the fan holiday. In 1979, a congratulatory ad in a London newspaper for Margaret Thatcher's election as prime minister used the line "May the Fourth be with you, Maggie. Congratulations."

holidays.name: International Respect for Chickens Day
holidays.description: This is a day to appreciate chickens, who are smarter, more social, and more expressive than their reputation suggests. Chicken fans celebrate by learning about chicken behavior, visiting sanctuaries, and thinking twice about the humble bird.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance, and its exact origin is unclear. It is observed by animal lovers and chicken enthusiasts as a way to highlight the personalities of these familiar farm birds.
holidays.funFact: Chickens can recognize dozens of individual faces, and hens start talking to their chicks before the eggs even hatch.

holidays.name: National Orange Juice Day
holidays.description: This day honors the sunny glass of OJ that has anchored American breakfast tables for generations. Raise a glass, squeeze a few oranges, or mix up a mimosa-style brunch for the occasion.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It celebrates America's most popular breakfast juice.
holidays.funFact: Orange juice is the most popular fruit juice in the United States, ahead of second-place apple juice.
